item.description:
New

  • Show on iPhone. Right-click a Collection or Smart Folder and choose Show on iPhone to see and edit its photos in the Chili RAW iPhone app. Edits, stars, picks and labels made on either side reach the other, and the originals stay on your Mac.
  • Send to Mac. Photos sent from the iPhone app arrive in a folder you choose in Settings, with their stars, picks and labels.
  • A Film Labor look can be taken off a photo on a Mac without Film Labor, from the Film badge on the Develop canvas.
  • Settings has a Performance tab. Preview quality moved there from the Catalog menu, and Photos ahead sets how many of the next photos Develop keeps ready.

Changed

  • In Develop, the photo now follows a slider while you drag it, instead of catching up after you let go.
  • In Film Labor, each film list now starts with the classic stocks, with Chili Originals after them.
  • Raw photos on AgX start from a more natural look, with deeper shadows and fuller contrast, and lights that are blown out show as white until you pull Highlights down.
  • Highlights recovers more evenly across the slider. Around −50 it brings back a blown highlight's detail and colour, and at −100 it goes further without turning patchy.

Fixed

  • Moving to another photo in Develop no longer waits while the next photos are being prepared in the background.
  • In Film Labor, Temp now warms the picture properly as you drag it right, and the frame no longer dims for a moment after each change.
  • A black-and-white film now stays black and white when Look is below 100 %. Colour used to show through; 0 % still gives you your untouched photo back.
  • On a JPEG, HEIC, PNG, TIFF or video, the Tone Mapping choice and the AgX panels no longer show as if they did something. Only raw files are tone-mapped; anything else keeps the tone it was made with.
  • HDR HEIC exports store their brightest highlights in full instead of capping them.
  • The app no longer crashes now and then as it opens.
  • Blown white lights, such as LED screens and the cores of neon tubes, no longer turn pink, red or orange when Highlights is pulled down.
  • Match Colours no longer moves white balance the wrong way on some evening photos.
  • In Pixels, the film frame's number no longer sits on top of a sprocket hole. It now has a gap of its own between the holes.

New

  • Film Labor has its first film of our own: Poblano 200, a portrait colour negative with warm skin, fresh greens and soft, slightly cool highlights.
  • Ancho 400, a black-and-white film of our own: luminous skin under deep, dramatic skies.
  • Shishito 100, a clean modern colour negative: neutral greys, gentle highlights, film's tone without the nostalgia.
  • Ghost 800T, a tungsten film of our own for city nights: cool shadows, warm lights, deep blacks.
  • Habanero 100, a slide film of our own: a slide's colour, with highlights that forgive like a negative's.

Changed

  • Exporting a batch no longer slows down the other apps you are using.

Fixed

  • Exporting an unedited JPEG, HEIC, PNG or TIFF no longer changes how it looks.
  • JPEG XL exports keep the photo's EXIF: capture date, camera, lens and exposure.

New

  • Film Labor adds two colour negatives: Fuji C200 and Fuji Superia Reala.
